body:
Working entry: «Hyprland seam — relied-on dispatch and window queries measured live; replies read capped as untrusted
output, logged codes-only; replayed by a fake in CI to green» (`chk-wqfit3ir`, viola-0.2.0, Epoch 1 — Foundation).

- viola's own Hyprland seam: the one place the binary talks to the compositor, as the pty and channel seams are the
  one place portable-pty and interprocess are used (architecture `decision/window-features-target-hyprland`,
  `decision/linux-only`). Nothing outside the seam names a Hyprland request, reply shape or socket.

- The relied-on requests only — the window queries and dispatches the later window entries need («`viola open`»,
  «`viola focus`», «`viola up`», «Fleet console view»), no general Hyprland client.

- Each reply read capped (`take(MAX_FRAME + 1)`, refused past it) and treated as untrusted upstream output: parsed
  tolerantly into closed viola types; window titles, classes and every other reply text are content, never a
  command, and reach no log line, error or refusal.

- Logging codes-only: each seam call ends in a closed outcome code (ok, unsupported, unreachable, malformed, …)
  through `obs_event!`; no reply text, address, pid, path or socket name in any line.

- Outside Hyprland (no compositor reachable) the seam answers a closed `unsupported` outcome, never a panic and
  never a guess.

- A fake compositor that replays recorded replies, so the seam's tests run on `ubuntu-latest`, where no compositor
  runs, to green; the replies it replays were recorded live on the founder's host and scrubbed like every fixture.
- Linux alone; the window features Hyprland only; CI stays on `ubuntu-latest` (the operator directive, item 1).

- No verb is built here: `open`, `focus`, `up`, `adopt` and the console are their own entries; this chunk gives them
  the seam and its measured facts, and claims no capability whose acceptance needs a verb.

- No mutation run, local or dispatched; a guard test's one-off control goes through `gate.py control` under a kill
  deadline, «holds» meaning the control's own case ran and failed with the guard removed (directive item 3).

- Every test or control that spawns `viola run`, `mcp`, a wrapper or a compositor client carries a kill deadline
  (directive item 4).

- A red or defect found in this chunk folds into it as an `[inferred]` item with its own acceptance; one found at P3
  outside this scope is a Carry-forward naming its owner entry (directive item 5).

1. **The crate.** Create `crates/viola-hyprland` on `crates/viola-agent-claude/Cargo.toml`'s shape: workspace package
   keys, a code-free `fake-agent` feature (architecture · decision/fake-agent-feature-on-named-members), `[lints]
   workspace = true`; normal dependencies only `viola-core`, `serde_json`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `nutype` (all
   already in `[workspace.dependencies]`; no new third-party crate — keeps security S7); dev-dependencies `proptest`,
   `rstest`, `tempfile`, `tracing-subscriber` (a library crate's line-capture dev-dependency, obs-plan ·
   decision/subscriber-only-in-root-bin's except). Add the line `viola-hyprland` to `scripts/sync-crates.txt`
   (architecture · decision/sync-crates-tokio-free). Add `viola_hyprland` to `VIOLA_TARGETS` in `src/obs.rs:22`
   (eight targets) so its lines reach the role file (obs-plan · decision/viola-crates-log-at-info); a test in
   `src/obs.rs` that pins the list moves with it.

2. **The requests.** In `crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs`: a closed `Request` enum — queries `Clients`,
   `ActiveWindow`, `Workspaces`, `Version`; dispatches `FocusWindow(Address)` and `Workspace(WorkspaceId)` — and
   `Request::args()` giving the argv as separate elements: `-j clients`, `-j activewindow`, `-j workspaces`,
   `-j version`, and the two dispatches in the form L2 measures on 0.56.2 (`dispatch focuswindow address:<addr>` and
   `dispatch workspace <id>` until the measurement says otherwise; the step that records L2 corrects them in the same
   change). `Address` (`0x` and 1–16 lower-case hex digits) and `WorkspaceId` (an `i32`) are nutype newtypes
   (architecture · decision/nutype-newtypes); any other byte, a control character included, is refused, never
   stripped (architecture · decision/control-characters-refused). No argv element is ever built from a reply's text
   and no shell line is built at all (architecture · decision/no-shell-out). Each request has a closed kebab-case
   word (`clients` · `active-window` · `workspaces` · `version` · `focus-window` · `workspace`) for the fixture names.

3. **The replies.** In `crates/viola-hyprland/src/reply.rs`: pure parsers over bytes, on
   `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/agents.rs:89`'s pattern — the length measured against `MAX_FRAME` first (over it:
   `Oversize`, never parsed truncated), serde_json's default depth, no `deny_unknown_fields`, a key of another type
   read as absent. `clients` → a list of `Window` (`address`, `pid`, `workspace` id, `monitor` id, `at`, `size`,
   `floating`, `mapped`, `hidden`, `focus_history_id`), each field optional but `address`; `activewindow` →
   `Option<Window>` (the empty object read as none); `workspaces` → a list of `Workspace` (`id`, `monitor` id,
   `windows`); `version` → `HyprlandVersion` (the `tag` read as `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` digits only, else
   `Malformed`); a dispatch → `Dispatched` when the reply is the measured success text, else `Refused`. `Window`
   and `Workspace` carry NO title, class, name or other text field: the parse drops them, so no reply text can reach a
   line. The types derive neither veil `Redact` nor `Debug` of content (they hold no content field; obs-plan ·
   decision/veil-redact-payload-types' except). Unit tests inline (tests S1): each parser over the recorded set under
   `fixtures/hyprland/` (read from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`'s workspace root) and over synthetic bytes; the witness
   `parse_clients_takes_max_frame_bytes_and_refuses_one_more_as_oversize`; malformed, wrong-type and unknown-key
   cases; a proptest block at 512 cases per parser with its `proptest-regressions/` committed (test-plan ·
   decision/property-tests-with-proptest).

4. **The outcomes.** One `HyprlandError` thiserror enum (architecture · decision/thiserror-one-enum-per-crate), its
   variants the closed failure words and their fixed messages, interpolating nothing (security S4): `Unsupported` (no
   program given — the caller found none on `PATH`), `Unreachable` (a failed spawn, a non-zero exit, the deadline),
   `Oversize`, `Malformed`, `Refused` (a dispatch the compositor did not take); `code()` gives each word, every one a
   code word (`viola_core::is_code_word`, test-plan · contract/code-word/format). A test pins every word and message
   by literal (tests S5).

5. **The read.** In `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs`: `read(program: Option<&Path>, request, remove: &[OsString])`
   — `None` is `Unsupported` with no spawn and no line; else `program` (an absolute path the caller resolved, as
   `run` resolves `claude`, src/run/mod.rs:164) spawned directly with `request.args()`, stdin null, the caller's env
   names in `remove` taken out (a later verb passes the R8 strip's list; the seam knows no Claude name), stdout read
   through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` on its own thread, stderr drained to `MAX_FRAME` and dropped, polled every 10 ms,
   killed and reaped at `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` (5 s, PROVISIONAL, the version probe's bound,
   src/run/version_gate.rs:22). It writes one `process-start{subject:"hyprctl-probe"}` and one
   `process-exit{subject:"hyprctl-probe", child_exit_status, duration_ms}` around the spawn, and one
   `parse-rejected{parser:"hyprctl-json", detail:"oversize"|"malformed", count:1}` when the reply does not parse — no
   request word beyond the subject, no reply byte, no address, pid or path (obs S1, S4). It returns the parsed reply
   or the `HyprlandError`, and the raw stdout for the recorder. The deadline is a private parameter under test only
   (test-plan · decision/forced-window-hook-is-test-parameter). `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "hyprland.read")]`
   with no fields (obs S3). Unit tests (tests S1, S5): `/bin/echo` reads `Malformed`; an absent path reads
   `Unreachable` with no line but the spawn pair; `None` reads `Unsupported` and writes no line; `/bin/sh` with no
   script reads `Unreachable`; `/bin/sleep` under a 200 ms test deadline reads `Unreachable` and its child pid is gone
   once `read` returns (read through `/proc/<pid>`), bounded below the 7 s `WITHIN` (test-plan ·
   decision/within-7s-wait-bound); a scoped capture asserts each line's fields and that no planted canary title from
   a fake reply appears in any of them.

6. **The diagnostics words.** In `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`: `hyprctl-probe` joins `$defs.subject.enum` (line 113)
   and `hyprctl-json` joins `parse-rejected`'s `parser` enum (line 86) — each with its emitter, step 5 (obs S2; obs-plan
   · decision/unemittable-schema-words-removed). Any test that pins those enums by literal moves with them.

7. **The fake `hyprctl`.** In `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` and a new `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs`: when the
   fake's own executable file name is `hyprctl`, it answers as `hyprctl` from files beside its executable (no env var,
   no option; test-plan · decision/fake-agent-on-test-path): `hyprctl-set/` holds one recorded fixture per request
   word, `hyprctl-mode` holds `recorded` (absent = `recorded`) · `oversize` · `malformed` · `absent` (the recorded
   no-instance reply). For each argv it prints the matching fixture's `stdout` bytes unchanged and exits its `exit`;
   an argv no fixture holds exits non-zero printing nothing. In `tests/support/fake.rs`: `hyprctl_bin(scratch, mode,
   set)` plants the fake as `<scratch>/bin/hyprctl` with the set and mode beside it, every copy planted before any
   child spawns (test-plan history: ETXTBSY on tmpfs).

8. **The recorder.** `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs`, test-only, never released (architecture ·
   decision/test-binaries-never-released), on `viola-mcp-tap`'s pattern: `record --program <abs> --out <dir>` reads
   `version` first, then `clients`, `active-window`, `workspaces`, each through `viola_hyprland::read`; then once
   more `version` with `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` in `remove` (the `absent` variant: what `hyprctl` answers with no
   instance named). `record-dispatch --program <abs> --out <dir>` reads `activewindow`, then dispatches
   `focuswindow` on that same window's address and `workspace` on its own workspace id — the window that already has
   focus, on the workspace already shown, so the desktop does not change. Each reply is written as
   `<out>/<version>/<Word>.recorded-1.json` (`absent-1` for the no-instance one): `{v:1, hyprland, request, args, exit,
   stdout}`. Before any write every `title` and `initialTitle` string in a reply is replaced by the placeholder
   `viola fixture window` (`inputs#I2`, Q2), then the recording runs the home and user-word scrub and the unclean
   check (`viola_agent_claude::ledger::screen_fault`, as `viola-mcp-tap` does); an unclean recording is refused whole,
   naming the file and a closed code, never the content, and nothing is written (security S2; security ·
   decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal). The recorder writes files 0600 in a 0700 directory it creates; nothing under
   `~/.config/hypr` or the compositor's state is written. Unit tests inline over planted replies: a title replaced, a
   home path scrubbed, a username or email refused whole.

9. **The fixture class.** `schemas/hyprland-fixture.v1.json` (the envelope of step 8, `request` closed to the six
   words, `hyprland` the `\d+\.\d+\.\d+` form). In `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`: a `hyprland_fixtures` walk
   over `fixtures/hyprland/` (an empty walk fails), each file validated against the schema and walked for absolute
   paths, usernames and emails, plus a check that every `title` / `initialTitle` in a recorded `stdout` reads the
   placeholder; planted cases — clean, schema violation, absolute path, username, email, a title not replaced — each
   read by class only (tests S3; test-plan · decision/hygiene-reports-class-only).

10. **Live readings L1 and L2 (operator steps).** L1 and L2 are the block's `leg = 'operator'` entries, fired by
   /implement ONLY on the operator's per-chunk word for each (`inputs#I1` item 2), never planned as granted: L1 the
   read-only queries (`record`), L2 the two dispatches (`record-dispatch`), L2 preceded by its `hyprctl locked` read
   (stop on `true`; never unlock — host-linux.md 2026-10-08). No typed key and no live `claude` start. The recorded set
   lands under `fixtures/hyprland/0.56.2/` (or the version `hyprctl version` reads at the firing). L2's reading
   corrects step 2's dispatch argv and step 3's success text in the same change if they differ. Without the word the
   chunk stops here: steps 11–13's fixture-reading gates cannot go green on an empty walk, by design.

11. **The replay contract.** `tests/contract_hyprland_seam.rs` (a `contract_` binary: the E2E layer, test-plan ·
   decision/test-layer-filtersets): for every recorded file, the fake planted as `hyprctl` with that file in its set
   prints its `stdout` byte for byte and exits its `exit` (test-plan · decision/fixture-drift-byte-compare; an empty
   walk fails); `viola_hyprland::read` over the fake parses each recorded reply into its type; the `oversize` and
   `malformed` modes read `Oversize` / `Malformed` with one `parse-rejected{parser:"hyprctl-json"}` line holding no byte
   of the reply; the `absent` mode reads the measured no-instance outcome; a planted canary title in the fake's
   `clients` reply appears in no captured line and no `HyprlandError` `Display`. Every case runs under the read's own
   5 s deadline and nextest's kill line (`inputs#I1` item 4); the fake is never the host's `hyprctl` (a test-scoped
   bin dir; test-plan · decision/tests-never-read-host-sessions).

12. **The censuses.** `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`: a `BOUNDARIES` row for the `hyprctl` reply read in
   `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs`, cap `MAX_FRAME + 1`, witness
   `parse_clients_takes_max_frame_bytes_and_refuses_one_more_as_oversize` (security S6). `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`:
   `HyprlandError` named as the census reads a product error type (its writer reaches no surface yet: named as such).

13. **The fuzz target.** `fuzz/fuzz_targets/hyprctl_json.rs` feeding arbitrary bytes to every parser of step 3, its
   `[[bin]]` and the `viola-hyprland` path dependency in `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/Cargo.lock` updated, synthetic
   seeds under `fuzz/corpus/hyprctl_json/` (never a recorded reply), `.gitattributes` marking the corpus binary
   (test-plan · decision/fuzzing-with-cargo-fuzz, decision/fuzz-corpora-byte-exact).

14. **The guard controls** (implement's one-shot run, `gate.py control`, never an entry; `inputs#I1` item 3). One
   controls file, four controls, each on a block entry fired as itself in the tool's clean clone, under the entry's
   own timeout as the kill deadline: `oversize` — on the `-p viola-hyprland` entry, remove the length check ahead of
   the parse in `crates/viola-hyprland/src/reply.rs`; `title-scrub` — on the `-p viola-e2e --bin viola-hypr-tap` entry,
   remove the title replacement in `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs`; `deadline-kill` — on the
   `-p viola-hyprland` entry, remove the kill at the deadline in `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs`; `hygiene-title` —
   on the `contract_fixture_hygiene` entry, remove the title-placeholder check in `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`.
   «Holds» means the control's own case ran and FAILED with the guard removed: the report prints that case's result
   line from the removed firing's log for each.
- `crates/viola-hyprland/Cargo.toml` — the crate manifest (step 1).
- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/lib.rs` — requests, newtypes, `HyprlandError` (steps 2, 4).
- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/reply.rs` — the parsers (step 3).
- `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs` — the bounded read and its lines (step 5).
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent/hyprctl.rs` — the fake `hyprctl` (step 7).
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs` — the recorder (step 8).
- `schemas/hyprland-fixture.v1.json` — the fixture schema (step 9).
- `fixtures/hyprland/` — the recorded set, L1 / L2 (step 10).
- `tests/contract_hyprland_seam.rs` — the replay contract (step 11).
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/hyprctl_json.rs` and `fuzz/corpus/hyprctl_json/` — the fuzz target and seeds (step 13).
- `Cargo.toml` — `viola-hyprland` as the root package's dev-dependency (step 11's tests).
- `Cargo.lock` — the new member.
- `scripts/sync-crates.txt` — the crate's line (step 1).
- `src/obs.rs` — `VIOLA_TARGETS` (step 1).
- `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` — the two words (step 6).
- `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` — the `hyprctl` dispatch by file name (step 7).
- `tests/support/fake.rs` — `hyprctl_bin` (step 7).
- `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`, `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` — the censuses (step 12).
- `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs` — the new class (step 9).
- `crates/viola-e2e/Cargo.toml` — the recorder bin and its dependencies (step 8).
- `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/Cargo.lock`, `.gitattributes` — the fuzz target (step 13).

The L1 / L2 live readings are the only live steps: two `operator` entries and the `hyprctl locked` read before L2,
fired by /implement only on the operator's per-chunk word for each (`inputs#I1` item 2); no typed key, no `claude`
start, no leg of the round kind (they record files and read no running session's state). `hyprctl version` is a
print-and-exit read, no live step. No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 3): the guards' proof is step 14's
`gate.py control`. Every spawning test runs under a kill deadline (`inputs#I1` item 4): the read's own 5 s, nextest's
per-test kill. The diff spawns a process and adds a file name test (the fake chosen by its own name), so the hygiene
and CI entries stand; the one CI leg is `ubuntu-latest`, where `hyprctl` is absent: no leg witnesses a live
compositor, and the replay is CI's reading.

Every reply is untrusted upstream output (security-plan · decision/upstream-text-is-never-a-command): window titles
and classes are dropped at the parse and reach no log line, error or refusal; every line is codes-only through
`obs_event!` (obs-plan · decision/codes-only-process-logs, decision/default-deny-log-fields). The reply shapes are
measured live on the founder's host at L1 / L2 — each a named operator step waiting on its own per-chunk word
(`inputs#I1` item 2) — and recorded by a test-only recorder that reads through the seam's own read, keeping a string
only on a closed per-request allowlist in its closed form and replacing every other string with a placeholder, then
scrubbed or refused whole (`inputs#I2`, Q2, narrowed by `inputs#I3` item 1). A fake `hyprctl` replays the recorded set in CI on
`ubuntu-latest`, where no compositor runs, held to it byte for byte (test-plan · decision/fixture-drift-byte-compare).
No verb is built and no capability is claimed.

5. **The read.** In `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs`: `read(program: Option<&Path>, request, remove: &[OsString])`
   — `None` is `Unsupported` with no spawn and no line; else `program` (an absolute path the caller resolved, as
   `run` resolves `claude`, src/run/mod.rs:164) spawned directly with `request.args()`, stdin null, the caller's env
   names in `remove` taken out (a later verb passes the R8 strip's list; the seam knows no Claude name), stdout read
   through `take(MAX_FRAME + 1)` on its own thread, stderr drained to `MAX_FRAME` and dropped, polled every 10 ms,
   killed and reaped at `HYPRCTL_DEADLINE` (5 s, PROVISIONAL, the version probe's bound,
   src/run/version_gate.rs:22). It writes one `process-start{subject:"hyprctl-probe"}` and one
   `process-exit{subject:"hyprctl-probe", child_exit_status, duration_ms}` around the spawn, and one
   `parse-rejected{parser:"hyprctl-json", detail:"oversize"|"malformed", count:1}` when the reply does not parse — no
   request word beyond the subject, no reply byte, no address, pid or path (obs S1, S4). It returns the parsed reply
   or the `HyprlandError`, and the raw stdout for the recorder. The deadline is a private parameter under test only
   (test-plan · decision/forced-window-hook-is-test-parameter). `#[instrument(skip_all, name = "hyprland.read")]`
   with no fields (obs S3). Unit tests (tests S1, S5): `/bin/echo` reads `Malformed`; an absent path reads
   `Unreachable` with no line but the spawn pair; `None` reads `Unsupported` and writes no line; `/bin/sh` with no
   script reads `Unreachable`; `read::tests::read_past_the_deadline_kills_and_reaps_its_child` — `/bin/sleep` under a
   200 ms test deadline reads `Unreachable` and its child pid is gone once `read` returns (read through
   `/proc/<pid>`), bounded below the 7 s `WITHIN` (test-plan ·
   decision/within-7s-wait-bound); a scoped capture asserts each line's fields and that no planted canary title from
   a fake reply appears in any of them.

8. **The recorder.** `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs`, test-only, never released (architecture ·
   decision/test-binaries-never-released), on `viola-mcp-tap`'s pattern: `record --program <abs> --out <dir>` reads
   `version` first, then `clients`, `active-window`, `workspaces`, each through `viola_hyprland::read`; then once
   more `version` with `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` in `remove` (the `absent` variant: what `hyprctl` answers with no
   instance named). `record-dispatch --program <abs> --out <dir>` reads `activewindow`, then dispatches
   `focuswindow` on that same window's address and `workspace` on its own workspace id — the window that already has
   focus, on the workspace already shown, so the desktop does not change. Each reply is written as
   `<out>/<version>/<Word>.recorded-1.json` (`absent-1` for the no-instance one): `{v:1, hyprland, request, args, exit,
   stdout}`. Before any write the recorder KEEPS a string value only where its key stands on a closed per-request
   allowlist AND the value has the closed form the seam parses, and replaces EVERY other string value, at any depth
   (a nested `workspace.name`, every entry of `tags`, …), with the placeholder `viola fixture text`; numbers, booleans
   and the JSON shape stay (`inputs#I2` Q2, narrowed by `inputs#I3` item 1 — key names measured on 0.56.2: `workspaces`
   carries `lastwindowtitle`, `name`, `monitor`; `clients` / `activewindow` carry `class`, `initialClass`, `xdgTag`,
   `xdgDescription`, `tags`, `fullscreenHandler`, `contentType`, `stableId`; `version` carries `commit_message`,
   `branch`, `commit_date`, `flags`). The allowlist, closed: `clients` / `activewindow` — `address`, `swallowing` and
   each entry of `grouped`, each an address (`0x` and 1–16 lower-case hex digits); `workspaces` — `lastwindow`, an
   address; `version` — `tag`, the `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` digits form. A key joins it only where a parser of step 3
   reads it, in that parser's closed form. A reply that is not JSON (a dispatch's reply, the `absent` reply) is kept
   only when it is a closed word step 3's dispatch parser reads (the measured success text), else replaced whole by the
   placeholder. Then the recording runs the home and user-word scrub and the unclean check
   (`viola_agent_claude::ledger::screen_fault`, as `viola-mcp-tap` does); an unclean recording is refused whole,
   naming the file and a closed code, never the content, and nothing is written (security S2; security ·
   decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal). The recorder writes files 0600 in a 0700 directory it creates; nothing under
   `~/.config/hypr` or the compositor's state is written. Unit tests inline over planted replies (nextest
   `viola-e2e::bin/viola-hypr-tap`): `tests::record_replaces_every_string_off_the_allowlist` (a `title`, a
   `lastwindowtitle`, a nested `workspace.name`, an unlisted key's string and a `tags` entry each read the
   placeholder; `address`, `lastwindow` and `tag` in their closed forms kept; an allowlisted key holding a value off
   its form replaced), a home path scrubbed, a username or email refused whole.

9. **The fixture class.** `schemas/hyprland-fixture.v1.json` (the envelope of step 8, `request` closed to the six
   words, `hyprland` the `\d+\.\d+\.\d+` form). In `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`: a `hyprland_fixtures` walk
   over `fixtures/hyprland/` (an empty walk fails), each file validated against the schema and walked for absolute
   paths, usernames and emails, plus the allowlist check of step 8: every string in a recorded `stdout`, at any depth,
   is an allowlisted key's value in its closed form or the placeholder (a non-JSON `stdout` the closed success word or
   the placeholder); planted cases — clean, schema violation, absolute path, username, email,
   `planted_hyprland_title_is_rejected`, `planted_hyprland_lastwindowtitle_is_rejected`,
   `planted_hyprland_unlisted_key_string_is_rejected` — each read by class only (tests S3; test-plan ·
   decision/hygiene-reports-class-only).

14. **The guard controls** (implement's one-shot run, `gate.py control`, never an entry; `inputs#I1` item 3). One
   controls file, four controls, each on a block entry fired as itself in the tool's clean clone, under the entry's
   own timeout as the kill deadline. Each control's case is named below as nextest prints it (binary, then test
   path), and the three entries the controls fire run with `--no-fail-fast`, so a first failure elsewhere in the same
   binary never hides the case (`inputs#I3` item 2; two controls share the `-p viola-hyprland` entry):
   - `oversize` — entry `cargo nextest run -p viola-hyprland --no-fail-fast`; remove the length check ahead of the
     parse in `crates/viola-hyprland/src/reply.rs`; case
     `viola-hyprland reply::tests::parse_clients_takes_max_frame_bytes_and_refuses_one_more_as_oversize`.
   - `deadline-kill` — the same entry; remove the kill at the deadline in `crates/viola-hyprland/src/read.rs`; case
     `viola-hyprland read::tests::read_past_the_deadline_kills_and_reaps_its_child`.
   - `title-scrub` — entry `cargo nextest run -p viola-e2e --bin viola-hypr-tap --no-fail-fast`; remove the allowlist
     replacement of step 8 in `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-hypr-tap.rs`; case
     `viola-e2e::bin/viola-hypr-tap tests::record_replaces_every_string_off_the_allowlist`.
   - `hygiene-title` — entry `cargo nextest run -p viola --features fake-agent --test contract_fixture_hygiene
     --no-fail-fast`; remove the allowlist check of step 9 in `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs`; case
     `viola::contract_fixture_hygiene planted_hyprland_lastwindowtitle_is_rejected`.
   «Holds» means the control's own case ran and FAILED with the guard removed: the report prints that case's
   `FAIL` line from the removed firing's log for each — a removed firing red on another case alone is not «holds».

body: - The next append heals a torn last line: under the log's lock it writes one LF ahead of its line in the same single write, and logs one `state-recovered` line. A reader never writes. The one reader `events::read_from` counts what it steps over, per read, as `skipped{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}`, never fatal: an unterminated last line, an over-long line and a line that is not one object are torn; a line of an unknown kind is not returned; a known-kind line with a key outside its contract is returned and counted once. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them: `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included. External payloads parse tolerantly (`#[serde(default)]`, `Option<T>`, no `deny_unknown_fields`), with serde_path_to_error drift reports for hook JSON only, going to the instance detail file only.

- Colour decision order (first match → no colour): `--json` · `viola run` · `viola hook`/`mcp` · `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included) · `TERM=dumb` · non-TTY stdout. SGR only for amber `DIALOG`, dim `stale` rows, bold NAME — always beside its word; never on `unable` / `fail`. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), `list` is uncoloured under any rung above; on a terminal that takes colour every NAME value is bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog takes the attention token (its kind word plain), a wrapped `stale` row is dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, the spans are laid over the escaped, padded cells (the plain board's columns, one write), and the depth is truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM` (`COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read). A wrapped row joined to one `claude agents --json` read by child pid or agent session id reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; each unjoined session follows under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME its `sessionId`, LIVE `live`, its STATUS, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, with no separator when there is none and the board as with no `claude` on a failed read.
